title: Noailles (Venice) to the Cardinal de Lorraine, 13 Nov 1558: BnF fr. 3151 no. 33

steps.what: Downloaded the Gallica volume fr. 3151 and located item 33 (views 60-61).

Found the court's decipherment in the inner margin beside each of the two cipher blocks on f. 60r; the binding hides the start of each gloss line ('... mauluaise ... gouvernement ... affaires'; '... grand seigneur ... ne luy ... de la fortune ...').

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): catalogue item 10 had grouped three letters in three different ciphers. La Guiche's 22-sign substitution stays in guiche1551; Noailles's Venice letter (another symbol alphabet) went to noailles1558 and Seure's six Lisbon letters (homophonic with numeral codes) to seure1558. The Noailles cipher itself was not transcribed or attacked.

Third cipher block (C, seven lines) found on f. 60v with a nearly complete decipherment of the time in the outer margin (Michael Brackx, issue #113; contributor step). Checked here on research/gallica_sweep/hi/k62.jpg (view 62): the block and the legible gloss lines are there. Extent corrected from two blocks, about 150 signs, to three blocks, 262 signs (his count).

Gloss readings on f. 60r corrected (Brackx, issue #113; contributor step), checked here on research/gallica_sweep/hi/k61_gloss.jpg: gloss A '...e pauur[ete]' and '[cond]uitte q[u'il] donne a', not 'gouvernement'; gloss B '[entre]prend sur luy et le' and 'de la Tou[ss]aint', not 'ne luy' and 'de la fortune'.

Key recovered from the three marginal glosses and a French 5-gram model (Montaigne): 246 of 262 tokens valued, 16 tentative; about 0.75 of words read on firm values (Brackx, issue #113; contributor step). Not reproduced here: no files attached; transcription, key, aligned decode and readings requested. His negative checks: fr. 3151 no. 14 in clear, Ribier II, fr. 20974 (31 Guise alphabets) none fits.

Brackx's crib_anneal.py (joint search of sign values and alignment with the marginal gloss) and lm_anneal.py (French 5-gram fill of free values), added to his gist on 28 Oct 2026 (revision d819ac655347), copied unchanged into brackx/ (MIT, credited). Not run here: lm_anneal.py needs numpy and a 5-gram table that is not in the gist, so the key recovery (246/262 valued in his first post) is still not reproduced.

Beling: Brackx's 272 sign tokens checked one by one on Gallica views 61-62 against his legend, shape only: 270 agree, 2 unclear, 0 differ; two pale possible extra signs (C4, A3). No decoded letter changes (beling/transcription_check.tsv).

Beling: Charrière, Négociations dans le Levant II (Internet Archive OCR) searched: Venice letters of 7 and 15 Nov 1558 printed, not this one of 13 Nov; no printed plaintext. The parallel cited as II 505 is in the letter of 7/20 Oct 1558, said of Ferdinand I (beling/charriere_check.md).

Beling: f. 60v C2, C4, C5 retried against the outer gloss (read 'ilz ont d'autruy les', '[vi]ennent p[ou]r a hazard'): tentative +o = z, Ob = r, lp = ost, ag possibly 'ay' in clear; C2 'u l', C4 'e r o' and C5 't h ?' still do not meet the gloss. No held-out test possible (key r5 used all glosses).

Brackx's gist (revision a026501dcb23) copied into brackx/ and his decode rebuilt here from his transcription and key r5 by our own check_brackx.py: all 272 sign tokens give the value in his decode file (the 2 differences of 274 are the bracketed clear words). 12 nulls, 260 non-null sign tokens, 244 with a value (93.8%), 12 of those on tentative values. His key recovery (crib_anneal.py, lm_anneal.py) was not rerun: the 5-gram table is not in the gist.

Integration of PR #423 after an independent verification: Beling's table has 274 rows (270 agree, 2 unclear, 2 possible extra signs) and its sequence matches Brackx's transcription 272 of 272; about 80 signs sampled on Gallica views 61-62 match their labels; the Charriere OCR hash and the p. 505 phrase (in the letter of 7 and 20 Oct 1558, about the emperor) confirmed; no letter of 13 Nov 1558 in Charriere II. Corrected here: the old Charriere citation in NOTES, and the '?' shown for '#' (= i) in nine rows of beling/transcription_check.tsv. Counts recounted from the files: 272 sign tokens, 76 labels, 12 nulls, 260 non-null, 244 valued (93.8%), 232 on firm values (89.2%), 12 tentative; legend.md's '256 valued' counts the 12 nulls. Profile brought into line with NOTES: the key was recovered by Brackx from the marginal decipherment (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext, contributed), text read in part. Read share measured on his reading with research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: 0.548 (51 words, 42 holes; every letter listed inside an unread stretch counts as a hole); with each unread stretch counted once, 51 words and 21 holes, 0.708. Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py, fr-1600-letters): reading -2.171 per letter, 200 random keys best -3.712, shuffled refit mean -2.447 and best -2.356: pass. The C2, C4 and C5 gaps stay open work: Beling's cribs from the gloss do not yet meet the decode.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 256 tokens, 61 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.171 per letter; random keys -4.597 (z 7.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.356 (mean -2.447, z 4.0); annealer on the real text -2.424. Verdict: pass.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Michael Brackx (issue #113, 27-28 Oct 2026) transcribed the three blocks and recovered the key by aligning the signs with the court's marginal decipherment (f. 60r inner margin, f. 60v outer margin) and filling the remaining values with a French 5-gram model. Here his decode was rebuilt from his transcription and key (272 of 272 sign tokens), his transcription was checked on the images by Andrew Beling (270 of 272 agree, 0 differ), and the reading passes the statistical validation; his key search itself was not rerun.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md (Brackx's reading of the three blocks, unchanged), research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py share: 51 words, 42 holes: 0.548. Tentative values, supplied letters and every letter listed inside an unread stretch count as holes. With each unread stretch counted once: 51 words, 21 holes, 0.708. Brackx's own figures: about 0.75 of words on firm values, 0.84 with the tentative ones. By signs: 244 of 260 non-null sign tokens have a value (93.8%), 232 on firm values (89.2%).

gaps.item: Start of each marginal gloss line on f. 60r, and with it the five large signs that open block B and the four after 'affaires' in block A
gaps.detail: swallowed by the binding; needs the page opened flat

gaps.item: f. 60v C2, C4, C5 unread groups: Beling's cribs from the outer gloss (11 Nov 2026) give tentative +o z, Ob r, lp ost, but C2 'u l', C4 'e r o' and C5 't h ?' do not meet the gloss as read
gaps.detail: open work, not only an image limit: the cribs exist and the decode does not yet meet them; next is a re-reading of gloss lines 4-8 (soft at Gallica's native resolution; a sharper image from the BnF would help) together with a re-look at the signs of those three stretches

gaps.item: 16 sign tokens of 15 labels without a value, and 12 tokens on tentative values (11 labels)
gaps.detail: each open label occurs once (zb twice) and each tentative value rests on one context; 272 signs give no second occurrence to test them

outcome.notes: Key recovered by Michael Brackx from the marginal decipherment of the time; text read in part (block A a full clause, block C a sentence with holes, block B fragments). No held-out test is possible: the key used all three glosses.

texts.label: The three cipher blocks, ff. 60r-60v
texts.summary: Three short passages in cipher inside a clear letter of Francois de Noailles, ambassador at Venice, to the Cardinal de Lorraine. Block A blames someone's 'bad order and poverty, or little conduct, that he gives to his affairs'; the subject is not in the cipher. Block B has someone who 'undertakes on him' and All Saints' Day; its opening signs are unread. Block C doubts that, for the singular pleasure and profit they have, 'they' come any bolder or better victualled; three stretches of it are open.
texts.note: Brackx's reading (issue #113), rebuilt here from his key and transcription. Read share 0.548 by v10_relabel (51 words, 42 holes), 0.708 with each unread stretch counted once; his own count is about 0.75 on firm values. The fuller file with the glosses and his notes is brackx/reading_original.md.

reading_review.note: Read as French: block A is one coherent clause that the gloss confirms word for word where it is legible (maulvaise, pauur[ete], [cond]uitte qu'il donne a ... affaires); block C builds one sentence with three unread stretches (C2, C4, C4-C5) and a doubtful end; block B is fragments around 'entreprand', 'sur luy et le' and 'le iour [de] la Toussaint'. Raw: the writer's spelling, no punctuation, line-broken. Not a full reading of any block but A.

prior.where: Contemporary decipherment in the inner margin of f. 60r, partly lost in the gutter, and in the outer margin of f. 60v (block C), nearly complete. The key was recovered from it.
